title: Multiplication formula for Hernandez and Leclerc's quivers with potentials

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper defines M[a,b] only for an i-box [a,b], which by Definition 2.2 requires i_a=i_b. It then sets M^{-\infty}:=\bigoplus_{a\in\mathbb Z_{<0}}M[a,0]. For a general admissible sequence, i_a is not equal to i_0 for every negative a, so [a,0] is not an i-box and M[a,0] is undefined for most summands. Consequently M^{-\infty}, its asserted rigidity, and End_A(M^{-\infty}) are not defined as written.

Proposition 2.1 states Ext-symmetry only for modules M,N over \widetilde\Pi that are locally free over \Pi(l) for some l. Immediately before Eq. (3.2), the paper claims that the isomorphism (2.4) yields Ext_A^1(M_1,M_2)\cong D Ext_A^1(M_2,M_1) for arbitrary A-modules M_1,M_2. An equivalence with graded \widetilde\Pi-modules does not make arbitrary modules locally free over a quotient \Pi(l). The hypotheses of Proposition 2.1 have been dropped. This unsupported symmetry is essential to the multiplication formula and later arguments.

predicted_errors.error_location: Lemma 3.1, final sentence of the proof
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: For fixed T'\subset M_1 and W'\subset M_2, the difference z_1-z_2 is a map T'\to M_2/W' satisfying the representation compatibility conditions. Thus the relevant translation space is Hom_A(M_1|_{T'},M_2/M_2|_{W'}), not the stated Hom_A(M_2,M_{1|W/W'}). The stated term reverses source and target and also uses W/W' as though W were a submodule of M_1. Therefore the displayed identification of the fiber is wrong, even though the fiber may still be an affine space for the correct reason.

The orthogonality relation E(M_1,M_2)^\perp_{T',W'}=E(M_2,M_1)_{W',T'} is imported from GLS07 for the appropriate preprojective/local-free setting, but the theorem is stated for arbitrary modules over the Jacobian-type algebra A. The paper supplies neither a nondegenerate Ext-pairing on all A-modules nor hypotheses that allow GLS07 to be transferred through \Phi. This is not repaired by Eq. (3.2), which itself was unjustifiably generalized from Proposition 2.1. Hence the correspondence-of-complements argument proving the multiplication formula does not apply as stated.

The specialization to dim Ext_A^1(M_1,M_2)=1 asserts F_{M_1}F_{M_2}=F_{Y_1}+F_{Y_2}. This requires, among other things, the reverse Ext-space also to have the required one-dimensional behavior and the two projectivized extension strata to consist of the asserted middle terms. Those facts rely on the invalid unrestricted Ext-duality. Moreover, Y_1 and Y_2 are described merely as modules 'subject to' exact sequences, rather than as the uniquely determined non-split middle terms. The displayed formula is therefore not established under the theorem's stated hypotheses.

The formula states F_{K_{i,r}^{(i)}} although the modules defined immediately beforehand are K_{k,r}^{(i)}, and the left-hand side depends on k. The correct F-polynomial must involve K_{k,r}^{(i)}. As written, the right-hand side has no k-dependence in its module index and cannot be the stated Hernandez--Leclerc formula.

The Kirillov--Reshetikhin highest monomial is written \prod_{j=0}^{k-1}Y_{i,r+j b_i}, but b_i is never defined anywhere in the paper. Earlier notation defines b_{ij} and d_i, and in the simply laced setup b_{ii}=2d_i. Thus the definition is mathematically ambiguous; if b_i was intended to be d_i, it has the wrong spectral step for the standard KR monomial.

The modules M_1,M_2 are repeatedly described as modules over A, but Proposition 4.3 and Lemma 4.4 use Ext_{\mathcal A}^1(M_1,M_2), where \mathcal A was defined as a cluster algebra (a commutative algebra), not the representation algebra A. No \mathcal A-module structures are defined for these representations. This makes the proposition and lemma ill-typed as written; the intended notation presumably was Ext_A^1.

The proof assumes without justification that if L_1\otimes L_2 is simple then there is a rigid A-module T with F_{M_1}F_{M_2}=F_T and g_T=g_{M_1}+g_{M_2}. Simplicity of a tensor product does not by itself imply that its simple class is a cluster monomial or has a rigid-module cluster-character realization. The subsequent inference that equality of F-polynomials and g-vectors produces one of two short exact sequences is also not a general consequence of those equalities.

The proof says that because T 'appears in the right hand' of the multiplication formula, 'we have Y=T for all Y' and hence F_T=2F_T. Neither assertion follows. F-polynomials of distinct modules are not asserted or known here to be linearly independent, and the multiplication formula is a sum over middle-term strata; the occurrence of T does not force every contributing middle term to be T. Thus the claimed contradiction and the 'only if' direction are invalid.

The proof only writes \chi_q^-(L_1\otimes L_2)=z^{g'}F_T+P and observes g'=g_1+g_2 from the unique dominant monomial. It then asserts, without a construction or theorem, that there is an exact sequence 0\to M_1\to T\to M_2\to0 or the reverse. Equality/additivity of g-vectors does not imply that the corresponding modules are related by an extension. The final conclusion that rigidity of T makes it the generic extension is likewise unsupported: rigidity alone does not establish that its orbit is the generic orbit within the relevant extension family.

The paper claims to establish a connection answering LM21, Conjecture 5.1 'in the sense of generalized preprojective algebras.' The stated conclusion rests on Theorem 4.5, whose proof does not establish the required extension or genericity assertions, and on Proposition 4.3/Theorem 3.2, both of which use unjustified unrestricted Ext-duality. Therefore the advertised resolution/answer substantially overstates what has been proved.
